findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the handsink along the main cookline. Shown to the PIC and soap was added to the dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Various salad dressings, potato salad, cut melon, and desserts were stored inside of a cooler with an ambient temperature of 50F. The foods were probed using several different internal thermometers. All TCS foods were discarded to correct the violation. The items had been stored in the unit since the morning, as far as the manager was aware. Ensure that TCS foods that are intended to be cold held are held at 41F or less. 

Also, ensure that shredded cheese that is being held on ice is changed frequently to avoid cheese from sitting in the temperature danger zone for long periods of time.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The cooler along the cookline that stores salad dressings had an ambient temperature of 50F. The inspector’s probe thermometer, the facility’s internal thermometer (recently placed inside of the unit), and the facility’s probe thermometer all verified an ambient temperature of 50F. The cooler stores salad dressing, uncooked broccoli, potato salad, fruit, and desserts. All time/temperature control(TCS) foods were pulled from the cooler and discarded. Per phone call with the facility’s manager, Don Hubbell, a service technician will be to service the cooler tomorrow morning. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain cold hold temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The handsink in the back slicing area is in need of caulking. The sink has pulled away from the wall and shall be recaulked to prevent debris accumulation. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the handsink in the front of the house. It appeared that the soap dispenser was empty. PIC replaced the dispenser with a new bag of soap to correct the violation. Be sure that hand soap is available at all handsinks to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of caulking:
- The dish table to the right of the dish machine is in need of recaulking. 
- The hand-sink to the right of the cook-line is in need of recaulking
Ensure that these areas are recaulked back to the wall to prevent the buildup of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Floors underneath equipment and counters are in need of a deep cleaning throughout the facility. Single service items, spilled liquids, food, and overall debris were observed on the floors throughout the kitchen and front of the house. PIC stated that employees tend to overlook the floors underneath and behind equipment when cleaning. Be sure to educate staff that when cleaning occurs, make sure to pull equipment (on wheels or available to be moved) from wall to thoroughly clean floors surrounding equipment.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the blade of the slicer to be soiled with food debris. PIC mentioned that the slicer is cleaned every day. Ensure that when cleaning the slicer, be sure to take apart (if possible) and clean machine parts so that the machine is cleaned thoroughly and free of debris. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Floors underneath equipment and counters are in need of a deep cleaning throughout the facility. Single services items, spilled liquids, and overall debris were on the floors of these areas.  Discussed with PIC. PIC is brand new and is just 3 days into the position. Ensure that floors underneath equipment and counters are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent build-up.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
The CFPM present for the inspection could not show proof of allergen training. Ensure that all CFMSa are allergen trained. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
